name: BeReal Design System
summary: Recreate BeReal's monochrome dual-lens capture UI: true-black canvas, draggable corner-snapping selfie inset, and honesty-first authenticity badges.
description: A production prompt for rebuilding BeReal's stripped-down, true-black photo ritual: the dual-lens composite card, the dual-shutter capture button, RealMoji reactions, and the 2-minute countdown banner, all rendered in system SF Pro with a single monochrome accent.

whatYouGet: A dark-only monochrome token set (true black canvas, white-only accent, single amber semantic color) plus the SF Pro type ramp
The dual-lens composite card spec — full-bleed back photo, draggable corner-snapping front selfie inset, and its capture/reaction siblings
Ready-to-paste SwiftUI-flavored guidance for the countdown banner, late badge, retake-count pill, and RealMoji cluster
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in stripped-down, anti-skeuomorphic interfaces. You have shipped photography and camera-first apps where restraint is the entire brand, and you default to system typography and a near-zero color palette rather than reaching for gradients or decoration.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color tokens (dark-only, no light mode):
- Canvas Black #000000 (true black, full-bleed, never a warm #121212)
- Surface 1 #1C1C1E (sheets, comment composer)
- Surface 2 #2C2C2E (elevated rows, chip backgrounds)
- Divider #2C2C2E
- Text Primary #FFFFFF, Text Secondary #8E8E93, Text Tertiary #636366
- Accent White #FFFFFF (the ONLY accent — there is no brand hue), On-Accent Black #000000
- Late Amber #FFD60A (reserved for lateness/urgency only)
- Error Red #FF453A, Online Green #30D158

Typeface ladder: system SF Pro Text/Display only, weights concentrated at 400/600/700 (no thin, no black, no custom face). Countdown numerals are tabular so digits never shift horizontally. Timer banner 24pt/700, screen title 22pt/700, username 17pt/600, caption 16pt/400, body 15pt/400, meta/timestamp 13pt/400, late badge 12pt/700.

Distinctive UI/interaction patterns:
1. Dual-Lens Composite Card — the atomic unit of the whole product: a 3:4 full-bleed back-camera photo (18pt corner radius) with a small 100x134pt front-camera selfie (14pt radius, 2pt black inner stroke) inset 12pt from the top-left corner, edge-to-edge in the feed (0pt side margins).
2. Draggable corner-snap selfie — long-press lifts the selfie inset (scale to 1.05 + shadow), drag, and release snaps it to whichever of the four corners it's nearest, via a spring (response 0.3, damping 0.75).
3. Dual-shutter capture button — a 76pt circle, 4pt white stroke, transparent center; on press a 64pt white disc fills in, paired with a heavy haptic for the back camera and a second, softer haptic roughly half a second later for the front camera.
4. RealMoji reaction cluster — real selfie photos (never abstract emoji), 30pt circles overlapping by 8pt, with zero numeric counts anywhere in the product.
5. Authenticity signaling as first-class UI — an inline "late" badge with a relative timestamp, and a small retake-count pill, both surfaced openly rather than hidden.
6. The 2-minute countdown banner — a blurred full-width pill at the top of the feed with tabular amber digits counting down, which flips its copy to a "late" prompt at zero.

Radius scale: 0pt (rare — avoided), 6pt (thumbnails), 14pt (selfie inset), 18pt (main card), 24pt (sheets), 500pt (full pill — buttons, countdown banner, comment composer), 50% (avatars/capture ring).
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never introduce a brand hue — white is the only accent color in the entire system, and amber exists solely for lateness/urgency, nothing else.
2. The canvas must be true #000000, never a softened warm black — the darkroom feel depends on maximum contrast.
3. The dual-lens composite (full photo + inset selfie) must be the hero of every surface it appears on — feed, profile grid, memories calendar — never replaced by a single flat photo.
4. The selfie inset is always draggable and corner-snapping; it must never be locked to one fixed position.
5. Never add like counts, follower counts, or any vanity metric — the retake count and late badge are the only numbers that matter, and they exist to be honest, not to flatter.
6. Reactions are always real selfie photos in a RealMoji cluster, never generic emoji, and never carry a count.
7. Shadows register through high opacity (0.6-0.8) and generous blur rather than darkening, because the canvas is already pure black — never invent a colored glow.
8. All primary/secondary buttons and the comment composer are full pills (500pt radius); avoid hard rectangles anywhere in the button system.
9. Respect the countdown's tabular-numeral requirement — digits must hold their horizontal position as they tick down.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App or feature name:
- Primary photo-ritual moment (e.g. daily capture, weekly check-in, a specific compliment/prompt cadence):
- Platform target (SwiftUI / React Native / Flutter / web):
- Screens in scope (capture, feed, profile grid, memories, settings, etc.):
- Any deviation from dual-camera capture (single camera, video, etc.):
- Existing brand constraints that must override BeReal's monochrome rule, if any:
- Target OS / minimum iOS version:
- Accessibility requirements beyond standard Dynamic Type and VoiceOver:
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete dark-only color token set (Swift `Color` extension or CSS variables) matching the reference palette, with a note on where each token is used.
2. A typographic scale definition (SF Pro sizes/weights/line-heights) covering timer, titles, usernames, captions, body, and badges, including the tabular-numeral treatment for the countdown.
3. The dual-lens composite card component, including the draggable/corner-snapping gesture logic for the selfie inset and its shadow treatment.
4. The capture button component with its press states, fill animation, and the two-stage haptic sequence.
5. The RealMoji reaction cluster and the late-badge/retake-count components, explicitly built with no numeric counts elsewhere.
6. The 2-minute countdown banner with its blur background, amber tabular text, and expiry state change.
7. A short responsive/orientation note confirming portrait-lock and how the selfie inset scales across the smallest and largest supported device widths.
</what_to_give_me>

whatYouGet: A three-theme (Light/Dim/Dark) color token map plus the SF Pro/Inter-parity type ladder
The skeet card anatomy and the pinned custom-feed selector, Bluesky's structural signature
The like pop-scale animation spec and the reply-controls composer chip
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer specializing in text-first social timelines. You have shipped multi-theme reading apps and understand how to keep a conversational feed calm and legible while still giving it one confident, joyful accent.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color tokens across three themes:
- Light: Canvas #FFFFFF, Surface 1 #F1F3F5, Surface 2 #E2E8F0, Divider #E2E8F0, Text Primary #0B0F14, Text Secondary #697787
- Dim: Canvas #1E2936, Surface 1 #27313E, Surface 2 #2E4052, Text Primary #F1F3F5, Text Secondary #9CA6B5
- Dark: Canvas #0B0F14, Surface 1 #161E27, Surface 2 #1E2936, Text Primary #F1F3F5, Text Secondary #8B98A5
- Bluesky Blue #1185FE (links, active tab, compose FAB, primary buttons), Blue Pressed #0F6FD6
- Like Red/Pink #EC4899 (the heart's filled state), Repost Green #2DBE85, Warning Amber #F5A623, Error #E5484D

Typeface ladder: system SF Pro on iOS with Inter as the cross-platform reference face, comfortable reading sizes concentrated around 15pt body at 1.4 line height. Weights run 400/500/600/700 — regular body, medium counts, semibold names/feed-tabs, bold large titles. Handles are always shown in full (never truncating the domain suffix).

Distinctive UI/interaction patterns:
1. Pinned custom-feed selector — a horizontally scrollable tab strip fixed at the top of Home (Following, Discover, plus any user-pinned algorithmic feeds), making the feed itself a switchable, user-owned object rather than one fixed algorithm.
2. Like pop-scale spring — tapping the heart fills it pink and pops from 1.0 to roughly 1.25 and back to 1.0 over about 300ms, paired with a light haptic and a count that rolls up.
3. Reply-controls composer chip — an inline chip on the compose sheet stating who is allowed to reply, turning blue when restricted, making the reply-gating model visible rather than buried.
4. Skeet card — flat, no elevation, separated from its neighbors by a single hairline divider rather than a bordered box or drop shadow.
5. Quote-skeet embed — a nested bordered card inside the body with its own 1pt border and rounded corners, distinct from a plain link-preview card.

Radius scale: 8pt (small chips), 12pt (media, link/quote embeds), 16pt (sheets/modals), 500pt (full pill — buttons, search field, feed-tab underline), 50% (avatars, FAB).
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Ship all three themes (Light, Dim, Dark) rather than a single light/dark pair — the choice of brightness is part of the product, not an afterthought.
2. Reserve Bluesky Blue for links, mentions, hashtags, the active tab, the compose FAB, and primary buttons only — body text is never tinted blue.
3. The like must be an animated pop-scale spring in pink, never a static color-swap toggle — the spring IS the personality of the interaction.
4. Keep the pinned custom-feed selector visible and reachable in one tap at all times; never demote it into a settings menu or secondary screen.
5. Always render the full handle including its domain suffix — never truncate or hide the back half of a username.
6. Keep cards flat and separate them with hairline dividers or thin embed borders; do not introduce drop shadows on ordinary skeet cards.
7. Surface the reply-controls chip on every compose flow so who-can-reply is always visible before posting, not hidden in a settings sheet.
8. Keep body text no smaller than 15pt at 1.4 line height — the app's voice is conversational and must stay comfortably readable.
9. Limit elevation to the compose FAB and modal sheets only — everything else on the timeline stays visually flat.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App or feature name:
- Primary content unit (short posts, long-form, mixed media, etc.):
- Platform target (SwiftUI / React Native / Flutter / web):
- Screens in scope (timeline, thread view, profile, compose, notifications, etc.):
- Theme requirements (all three, or a subset):
- Feed/algorithm model (single feed vs. multiple switchable feeds):
- Existing brand color that should replace or sit alongside Bluesky Blue, if any:
- Accessibility requirements beyond standard Dynamic Type:
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete three-theme color token set (Light/Dim/Dark) as a Swift `Color` extension or CSS variable map, annotated with which surface each token belongs to.
2. A typographic scale (sizes/weights/line-heights) for screen titles, skeet body, handles, feed-tab labels, and action counts.
3. The skeet card component: avatar, name/handle/timestamp header, body with tinted links, embed slot, and the evenly spaced action row.
4. The pinned custom-feed selector component with its selected-state underline and cross-fade transition between feeds.
5. The like button component with its full pop-scale animation timeline and haptic trigger.
6. The compose sheet including the reply-controls chip and its restricted/open visual states.
7. A short note on how the three themes should be toggled (system-driven vs. explicit in-app switch) and how the switch itself should animate.
</what_to_give_me>

summary: Recreate Clubhouse's warm cream-paper audio-room UI: serif titles, circular avatars, and the emerald speaking-ring pulse.
description: A production prompt for rebuilding Clubhouse's literary-salon audio-room interface — cream/warm-black surfaces, DM Serif Display titles paired with Inter UI text, and the emerald speaking-ring halo that is the app's entire 'now playing' signal.

whatYouGet: A warm cream-and-emerald token set (light 'hallway' + warm-dark 'room' surfaces) and the serif/sans type pairing
The speaker-avatar component with its idle/speaking/muted/host states and the breathing emerald halo
The live-room stage layout, hand-raise footer, and Hallway list-card patterns
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in warm, editorial, voice-first social products. You favor paper-like surfaces, serif display type, and calm, human-voiced micro-copy over cold tech-blue conventions.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color tokens:
- Cream Hallway (light canvas) #F2EFE4, Cream Card #FBF9F1, Cream Pressed #EAE6D8, Divider #DDD8C8
- Dark Room (warm near-black canvas, NOT slate) #1A1A1A, Dark Surface 1 #242220, Dark Surface 2 #2E2B27, Dark Divider #3A372F
- Ink (text on cream) #1A1A1A, Ink Secondary #6B6453, Cream text-on-dark #F2EFE4
- Speaking Emerald #38B569 (the single accent), Emerald Deep (pressed) #2E9A58, Emerald Soft/pulse #38B569 at 18% opacity
- Moderator Gold #E9C46A, Leave/Error #E5575C (or #D9534F on light)
- Avatar gradient palette (assigned deterministically per user): Peach #F4C77B→#E0A24B, Sage #9FD8B4→#5FB484, Lavender #C9B6E8→#9C7FD0, Coral #F2A9A0→#D9776B, Sky #A9C7E8→#6E9CD0

Typeface ladder: DM Serif Display for every title/topic/greeting/pull-quote (28pt room title, 24pt screen title, italic 20pt pull-quotes) paired with Inter for every piece of interactive UI (names, roles, buttons, metadata) at weights 400/600/700 only. Only tiny group overlines are set in uppercase; everything else uses warm sentence case, and emoji are treated as first-class inline glyphs in button and title copy.

Distinctive UI/interaction patterns:
1. Speaking-ring pulse — a circular avatar gains a 3pt solid emerald ring plus a soft breathing halo (roughly 1.0 to 1.12 scale on a ~0.9s loop) the instant that person is talking; this is the app's only "now playing" indicator, with no waveform or color fill substitute.
2. Room stage as grouped speaker grid — avatars organized under uppercase overlines (Speakers / Followed by the speakers / Others in the room) rather than a chronological feed.
3. Raise-hand footer control — a soft pill reading an emoji-led "raise hand" label that flips to a confirmed "hand raised" state once tapped, with moderators seeing a queue tray of everyone waiting.
4. Role state read at a glance — a host pin badge, a gold-tinted name for moderators, and roughly 55% opacity plus a small mute badge for muted speakers, with no additional labeling needed.
5. Stacked avatar cluster — 3 to 5 circular avatars overlapping by about 10pt used for room previews and "and N others" rows, capped with a trailing count chip.
6. Mini room bar — a collapsed room docks as a thin pill above the tab bar carrying the truncated title and the live speaker's still-pulsing avatar.

Radius scale: 8pt (small chips), 16pt (Hallway cards, sheets), 24pt (onboarding/modal sheets), 500pt/full pill (essentially every button, status badge, and search field), 50% (every avatar, mute badge, host pin, speaking ring).
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. The canvas must be warm — cream paper on light, a warm near-black on dark — never pure white or a cold blue-gray slate in either mode.
2. Every title, room topic, and greeting is set in the serif display face; every name, role, button, and metadata string is set in the sans — never mix the two registers on the same content.
3. The emerald speaking ring plus its breathing halo is the ONLY way to show who is talking — never substitute a waveform bar or a flat color fill.
4. Treat the emerald accent as precious: it appears only for the speaking state, the primary CTA, and "open" room status — never as general decoration.
5. Every avatar is a perfect circle and every button, badge, and search field is a full pill — the system essentially avoids hard rectangles entirely.
6. Muted participants dim to roughly 55% opacity plus a small mute badge; hosts get a pin badge; moderators get a gold-tinted name — these are the only role signals needed, with no extra text labels.
7. Keep the voice gentle in all copy — an exit action reads as calm ("leave quietly") rather than an alarming red "exit" button.
8. Keep the speaking pulse slow (roughly a 0.9-second breath) — never a fast strobe — and keep sheet transitions and other motion equally unhurried.
9. Group the room stage under clear overlines (Speakers / Followed by speakers / Others) rather than presenting one undifferentiated grid of faces.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App or feature name:
- Primary live-audio format (rooms, clubs, scheduled events, etc.):
- Platform target (SwiftUI / React Native / Flutter / web):
- Screens in scope (live room, hallway/discovery list, profile, scheduling, etc.):
- Roles to support beyond host/speaker/listener, if any:
- Existing brand accent that should replace or sit beside the emerald, if any:
- Target OS / minimum iOS version:
- Accessibility requirements beyond Dynamic Type and Reduce Motion:
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete cream/warm-dark color token set (Swift `Color` extension or CSS variables) plus the avatar gradient palette.
2. A typographic scale pairing the serif display sizes with the Inter UI sizes, noting exactly which content gets which face.
3. The speaker-avatar component with its idle, speaking (ring + breathing halo), muted, and host states fully specified.
4. The room stage layout — grouped sections, grid density, and how it reflows across phone and tablet widths.
5. The hand-raise footer control and its tap animation, plus the moderator queue tray it opens into.
6. A Hallway-style discovery list-card component with its stacked avatar cluster and status pill.
7. A short note on how the mini room bar should behave when a room is collapsed and re-expanded.
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in high-density, card-based information feeds for very large, mixed-demographic audiences. You default to function-first layouts, generous labeling, and a restrained but purposeful use of color to signal role rather than to decorate.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color tokens:
- Canvas Gray (light) #F0F2F5, Card White #FFFFFF, Surface Tint #F7F8FA, Divider #E4E6EB
- Dark Canvas #18191A, Dark Card #242526, Dark Surface Tint #3A3B3C, Dark Divider #3E4042
- Text Primary (light) #050505, Text Primary (dark) #E4E6EB, Text Secondary #65676B / #B0B3B8, Text Tertiary #8A8D91
- Facebook Blue #1877F2 (brand, nav f-mark, active Like, primary CTAs, links), Blue Pressed #0A5FC8, Blue Light tint #E7F3FF
- Reactions palette: Like Blue #1877F2, Love Pink #F3425F, Care/Haha/Wow/Sad amber #F7B928, Angry Orange #E9710F
- Live Red #FA3E3E, Error Red #FA383E, Success/Create Green #42B72A
- Story ring gradient (inherited): #C13584 → #E1306C → #FD1D1D → #F77737

Typeface ladder: system SF Pro throughout (no custom brand face), weights concentrated at 400/600/700/900, with 900 reserved solely for the "f" logo glyph. Post body reads at 15pt/400, display names at 15pt/600, section headers at 20pt/700, screen titles at 24pt/700 — large display type is rare because the feed has to accommodate ten-plus distinct content types without shouting.

Distinctive UI/interaction patterns:
1. Card-based feed — every post, ad, and suggestion lives in its own white rounded-rectangle card (8pt radius) floating on the soft-gray canvas, separated by an 8pt gap rather than hairline dividers.
2. Reactions popover — long-pressing the Like button opens a horizontal floating pill of seven reaction icons; dragging across them scales the hovered one up with a tooltip label, and releasing swaps that reaction into the action row.
3. Five-tab labeled bottom bar — Home, Video, Marketplace, Notifications, Menu, each tab always paired with a visible text label (not icon-only).
4. Stories row — 110x200pt rounded rectangles with a gradient ring for unread stories, inherited visually from Instagram's story-ring treatment.
5. Reaction summary strip — a row of small stacked reaction-icon circles plus a plain-text "you and N others reacted" line, sitting above a divider and the action row.
6. Comment threading — nested replies indented from their parent with a thin vertical rule connecting them, inside rounded comment bubbles.

Radius scale: 6pt (Add Friend/Friends pills), 8pt (post cards, CTA buttons), 12pt (story thumbnails), 16pt (comment bubbles), 20pt (comment input pill), 500pt (reactions popover, "What's on your mind" pill, search bars), 50% (avatars, reaction icons, nav icon buttons).
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Put every feed item in its own white (or dark-card) rounded rectangle floating on the gray canvas — this is the single most card-based of the social layouts and should stay that way.
2. Reserve Facebook Blue for the brand mark, the active Like state, primary CTAs, and links — never spread it across incidental UI.
3. Never collapse the seven-reaction system down to a single heart or thumbs-up-only model — Like, Love, Care, Haha, Wow, Sad, and Angry must all be reachable via long-press.
4. Keep all five bottom-tab labels visible at all times — this app is deliberately label-forward rather than icon-only.
5. Rely on the gray-canvas/white-card contrast for elevation instead of heavy drop shadows on ordinary post cards.
6. Reserve the success green strictly for creation actions (Create Post, List for Sale) — never use it as a general primary accent.
7. Keep the top nav white or dark-card with a blue f-mark rather than reverting to a solid blue top bar — the blue bar is a deprecated historical pattern.
8. Use SF Pro at weights 400/600/700/900 only, with 900 reserved for the f-mark — no thin or light weights anywhere.
9. Keep story thumbnails as tall rounded rectangles (never square) with the inherited gradient ring on unread items.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App or feature name:
- Primary content types in the feed (text posts, photos, links, marketplace listings, events, etc.):
- Platform target (SwiftUI / React Native / Flutter / web):
- Screens in scope (feed, stories, profile, marketplace, notifications, comments, etc.):
- Tab bar structure if different from the five-tab default:
- Reactions set (full seven, a subset, or a custom set):
- Existing brand color that should replace or sit beside Facebook Blue, if any:
- Accessibility requirements beyond standard Dynamic Type:
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete light/dark color token set (Swift `Color` extension or CSS variables) including the full reactions palette.
2. A typographic scale for screen titles, section headers, post body, comment body, and button labels.
3. The post-card component: header row, body text, optional media, reaction summary, and the action row.
4. The long-press reactions popover with its open animation, drag-hover scaling, and haptic sequence.
5. The five-tab labeled bottom bar with active/inactive states and the notifications badge treatment.
6. The stories row component including the gradient unread ring and the "create a story" first-card state.
7. A short note on comment-thread nesting depth and how the connecting rule should render for deeply nested replies.
</what_to_give_me>

name: Flickr Design System
summary: Recreate Flickr's photographer-first gallery UI: the justified photo mosaic, a five-point favorite star, and a prominent EXIF metadata table.
description: A production prompt for rebuilding Flickr's gallery-wall design system — a near-black canvas, a row-packed justified photo grid, twin brand-dot colors, and the camera-metadata (EXIF) table that no other mainstream photo app surfaces so prominently.

whatYouGet: A near-black gallery token set with the twin Flickr Pink/Blue accent pair and a serif-plus-sans-plus-monospace type system
The justified photo-mosaic layout algorithm and the photo-detail page anatomy, including the EXIF table
The five-point favorite-star component and tappable camera/lens metadata chips
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer specializing in photography-first gallery apps. You understand row-packing mosaic layouts, EXIF/camera metadata presentation, and how to keep chrome invisible so full-color photography reads first.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color tokens:
- Gallery Canvas (dark, default) #0C0D0E, Surface 1 #1A1B1D, Surface 2 #232427, Divider #2A2C30
- Canvas White (light) #FFFFFF, Surface Gray #F5F6F7, Surface Pressed #EAECEF, Divider Light #E2E4E8
- Text Primary #FFFFFF (dark) / #1C1F23 (light), Text Secondary #B0B3B8 (dark) / #6B7077 (light), Text Tertiary #6E7176
- Flickr Pink #FF0084 (favorites + primary actions), Pink Pressed #D60070
- Flickr Blue #0063DC (links + secondary actions), Blue Pressed #0052B8
- Pro Gold #FFB200 (Pro-badge only), Success #00C781, Error #FF3B5C, photo scrim rgba(0,0,0,0.45)

Typeface ladder: Proza Libre (an editorial serif) for titles, photo titles, and section headers (32pt/700 screen title down to 18pt/600 photo title); Inter for all functional UI (body, metadata, buttons, EXIF labels); and a monospace face (SF Mono / IBM Plex Mono) exclusively for EXIF values so figures like f/2.8, 1/250s, and ISO 100 align in fixed-width columns like a camera readout.

Distinctive UI/interaction patterns:
1. Justified photo mosaic — a row-packing algorithm that scales each photo by its native aspect ratio so every row fills the screen width at a consistent target height, with no cropping and a very tight 3pt gutter between tiles.
2. EXIF / camera detail table — a titled key-value card on the photo-detail page listing Camera, Lens, Exposure, Aperture, Focal length, ISO, and Date taken, with monospace right-aligned values; camera and lens rows are tappable and open a "more shot with this gear" search.
3. Five-point favorite star — deliberately not a heart; fills solid pink when active, with a spring pop-scale and a soft haptic on tap.
4. Twin brand-dot accent system — Flickr Pink for favorites and primary actions, Flickr Blue for links and secondary actions, with no other chromatic accent anywhere except a Pro-only gold star.
5. Tappable camera/lens/keyword chips — pill-shaped tags on the detail page that open a filtered search for "more shot with this gear."
6. Shared-element grid-to-detail transition — a tapped mosaic tile expands into the full-width detail image via a matched geometry transition rather than a plain push.

Radius scale: 0pt (grid tiles, full-bleed detail image — deliberately square-cornered), 2pt (inline thumbnails), 4pt (small badges), 6pt (buttons), 12pt (EXIF table card, album sheets), 16pt (bottom sheets), 500pt (Follow pill, tag chips), 50% (avatars).
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Keep grid tiles and the full-width detail image square-cornered, borderless, and shadowless — the gallery wall must read as continuous, with no rounding or drop shadows competing with the photography.
2. Build the main feed as a justified, row-packed mosaic that preserves each photo's native aspect ratio — never crop or letterbox to force a uniform grid.
3. The favorite/like primitive is always a five-point star, never a heart, and it fills solid pink when active with no numeric "like" wording.
4. Surface the EXIF/camera-metadata table prominently on every photo-detail page — this is Flickr's core identity, not an optional secondary screen.
5. Set every EXIF value in the monospace face so decimal points and units align in a column; never use a proportional font for camera readouts.
6. Restrict chromatic accents to exactly two brand colors — pink for favorites/primary and blue for links/secondary — with the gold star reserved strictly for Pro badges.
7. Use the editorial serif only for titles and section headers; never set EXIF labels, tab labels, or button text in the serif.
8. Keep the tight 3pt gutter in the photo grid — do not widen it, since the density of the mosaic is the signature layout trait.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer specializing in joyful, game-like social apps for teen audiences. You favor bright gradients, heavy rounded type, and springy celebratory motion over restrained corporate minimalism, while keeping every interaction safe, positive, and finite.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color tokens:
- Brand gradient (the entire app background) #6C5CE7 → #A06CFF, Gas Indigo #6C5CE7, Gas Purple #A06CFF, Gas Violet (on-white tint) #7B4DFF
- Card White #FFFFFF, Tint Surface #F4F2FF, Divider #ECE9FB, Glass Bar rgba(255,255,255,0.16), Scrim rgba(40,20,90,0.45) — always purple-tinted, never gray-black
- Card text: primary #1A1530, secondary #6B6588, tertiary #A29DB8
- Fixed festive choice-button palette (rotates per poll slot): Indigo #6C5CE7→#8B6CFF (white text), Pink #FF6CC8→#FF9CDB (white text), Yellow #FFC93C→#FFB13C (text #4A3300), Green #2BC48A→#4FD9A6 (white text)
- Flame currency #FF7A45, Flame Glow rgba(255,122,69,0.15), Success #2BC48A, Error #FF5470

Typeface ladder: Nunito, a rounded friendly sans, run deliberately heavy — almost everything sits at 800 (ExtraBold) or 900 (Black), with regular 400 barely used anywhere. Poll questions run 23pt/900 centered, choice-button labels 16pt/800, big numbers (flame counts) 28pt/900. A 50pt emoji crowns nearly every poll card and is treated as part of the headline.

Distinctive UI/interaction patterns:
1. One floating white poll card at a time — no feed, no infinite scroll; the entire core loop is a single centered card per screen.
2. Anonymous compliment poll — an emoji headline plus a bold centered question plus four gradient name buttons locked into a strict 2x2 grid (never 1x4 or a list), with every question framed as a positive compliment.
3. Flame currency loop — flames are earned by voting and spent to unlock "who picked you" hints, with the running count living in a glowing pill and animating digit-by-digit when it increases.
4. Shuffle and skip controls — a reshuffle affordance swaps which names occupy the four slots, and a skip control advances to the next card without answering.
5. Purple-tinted shadows everywhere — every drop shadow in the system uses a plum/purple tint rather than neutral gray or black, keeping elevation cohesive with the gradient world.
6. Segmented progress dots — a row of small pill segments below the poll card shows position within the current set, widening the active segment.

Radius scale: 8pt (progress-dot segments), 14pt (small inner panels), 20pt (the four choice buttons, generic cards), 28pt (the hero poll card), 36pt (bottom sheets), 500pt/999pt (primary CTAs, the flame pill, search), 50% (the raised center tab action, avatars).
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. The world background is always the full-bleed indigo-to-purple gradient — this is a light-UI-by-design product and should never ship a dark theme.
2. Show exactly one poll card centered on screen at a time — no feed, no infinite scroll, no list of past polls competing for attention.
3. Every poll question must read as a compliment — never negative, never comparative in an unkind way; the tone is unconditionally positive.
4. Lock the four choice buttons into a strict 2x2 grid using the fixed festive palette by slot (indigo/pink/yellow/green) — never rearrange them into a 1x4 list.
5. Reserve flame-orange strictly for the currency system (earning, unlocking hints) — it must never be reused for any other meaning.
6. Set type heavy throughout — nothing below weight 700, with body copy and most UI sitting at 800-900; this chunkiness is the entire brand voice.
7. Tint every shadow toward purple/plum rather than neutral gray or black, so elevation feels part of the gradient world rather than a generic iOS default.
8. Keep the experience finite and phone-shaped even on tablets — the poll card stays centered with a capped max-width rather than spreading into a multi-column grid.
9. Keep real names and photos out of the poll-selection moment itself — anonymity during voting is a safety feature, not a limitation to work around.
</house_rules>

</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete gradient-world color token set (Swift `Color`/gradient definitions or CSS variables) including the four-slot choice palette and the flame accent.
2. A typographic scale confirming the heavy 800/900 weight distribution across display, poll question, choice button, and big-number roles.
3. The poll-card component: emoji headline, question, tag line, 2x2 choice grid, and shuffle/skip footer controls.
4. The flame-currency pill component with its digit-by-digit count-up animation and haptic.
5. The "who picked you" reveal card, including the locked/blurred hint rows and the unlock-for-flames interaction.
6. The segmented progress-dots component and its active/inactive states.

</what_to_give_me>

The icon-only tab bar and stories-ring component, including the unread conic-gradient ring treatment
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer specializing in content-first, chromatically restrained interfaces. You know how to make chrome disappear so photography and video are the only colorful thing on screen, and you understand exactly how sparingly a signature brand gradient should be spent.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color tokens:
- Pure Black #000000 (dark canvas / light-mode text), Pure White #FFFFFF (light canvas / dark-mode text)
- Secondary Gray #8E8E8E (light) / #A8A8A8 (dark), Separator #DBDBDB (light) / #262626 (dark)
- Link Blue #00376B (light) / #E0F1FF (dark) — deeper/navy-leaning, not system blue
- Primary Action Blue #0095F6 (Follow/Log in/Sign up only), Pressed #1877F2
- Destructive/Liked Red #ED4956
- Brand gradient (10-stop, bottom-left to top-right): #FFDC80 → #FCAF45 → #F77737 → #F56040 → #FD1D1D → #E1306C → #C13584 → #833AB4 → #5851DB → #405DE6, with a 3-stop shorthand #833AB4 → #FD1D1D → #FCAF45 used in tighter UI moments
- Online Green #78DE45, Close Friends Green #2FB825

Typeface ladder: system SF Pro Text exclusively for UI, with a proprietary script logotype used only once at the top of the Home feed and never in body text. No display-size type exists anywhere in the app — the biggest text is the 28pt logotype. Weights concentrate at 400/600/700 with semibold (600) carrying nearly all emphasis; usernames are always the most emphasized element in any row.

Distinctive UI/interaction patterns:
1. Reserved brand gradient — the 10-stop (or 3-stop shorthand) gradient appears in exactly three places: the app icon/logotype, unread stories rings, and the Create/Reels action — never on ordinary buttons, text, or decorative fills.
2. Icon-only tab bar with no text labels at all (removed by design), trusting the outline glyphs to be self-explanatory.
3. Edge-to-edge, zero-corner-radius media — every feed photo, grid tile, and Reel bleeds to the device edges with no rounding, ever.
4. Double-tap-to-like — a large heart springs from 0 to roughly 1.4 scale and fades out over the image center, paired with a soft haptic, independent of the smaller heart icon in the action bar.
5. Story ring as status indicator — a 2.5pt conic brand-gradient stroke means unread, collapsing to a plain 1pt gray stroke once viewed.
6. Tight 2pt grid-tile gutter on the profile/explore grid — noticeably tighter than typical iOS grid spacing, reinforcing that chrome should recede.

Radius scale: 0pt (all feed/grid/story media — non-negotiable), 4pt (small badges), 8pt (buttons, follow pills), 10pt (search bars), 20pt (DM bubbles), 50% (avatars, story rings, icon hit targets).
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Keep every piece of chrome strictly monochrome (black, white, gray) — if a control or icon is tinted anything other than the single action blue or the destructive red, reconsider it.
2. Treat the brand gradient as scarce: it belongs only on stories rings, the Create/Reels action, and the logotype/app icon — never on a general button, badge, or text fill.
3. Never round the corners of feed photos, grid tiles, or Reels — edge-to-edge squares and portraits with zero radius are a hard rule, no exceptions.
4. Do not add text labels to the tab bar — it is icon-only by design, with outlined glyphs for inactive and filled glyphs for the active state.
5. Cap all UI type under 20pt except the fixed 28pt logotype — there are no display-size headlines anywhere in this system.
6. Use `#0095F6` for exactly one purpose — the single "take action" button (Follow, Log in, Sign up) — and nowhere else.
7. Keep feed content on a single flat z-plane; do not add drop shadows to ordinary post cards, only translucent blur materials on the nav/tab chrome and sheets.
8. Use true `#000000` for dark mode, not a softened dark gray, to preserve both the OLED-efficiency rationale and the stark monochrome identity.
9. Pair every like, save, and follow action with a light, subtle haptic rather than a heavier or more theatrical one.
</house_rules>

</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete light/dark monochrome color token set (Swift `Color` extension or CSS variables) plus the full 10-stop gradient definition and its 3-stop shorthand.
2. A typographic scale confirming the sub-20pt cap on UI type and where the one fixed-size logotype sits.
3. The feed-post component: header, zero-radius media, action bar, like-count/caption block, and comment preview.
4. The double-tap-to-like heart animation and the smaller in-row like icon's fill/spring behavior.
5. The icon-only tab bar component with active/inactive glyph states and the long-press account-switcher gesture.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer specializing in editorial, magazine-style discovery feeds. You think in masonry layouts, pastel color systems, and typographic pairings that separate a friendly display headline face from a clean reading-body face.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color tokens:
- Canvas White #FFFFFF, Surface 1 #FAFAFA, Surface 2 #F2F2F2, Divider #ECECEC
- Dark Canvas #121212, Dark Surface 1 #1C1C1E, Dark Surface 2 #2A2A2A, Dark Divider #2E2E2E
- Ink/Text Primary #1A1A1A, Text Secondary #6B6B6B, Text Tertiary #9A9A9A
- Lemon8 Yellow #FFE600 (used sparingly, always paired with ink text, never white-on-yellow), Yellow Pressed #E6CF00
- Pastel topic tags: Mint bg #E4F5EC / text #1F8A52, Blush bg #FCE8EE / text #C13E68, Sky bg #E6F0FB / text #2D6FB8, Butter bg #FFF6CC / text #8A7300, Lavender bg #F0EAFB / text #7050B0
- Like Red #FF2E63, Success #1FB877, Error #FF3B5C, photo-chip scrim rgba(0,0,0,0.55)

Typeface ladder: Poppins (a geometric, rounded display face) for large screen headers, tab headers, and post titles (32pt/800 down to 18pt/600); Inter for everything functional — card titles, body copy at 16pt/400 with 1.55 line height, metadata, tags, and tab labels. Card titles are short, punchy, line-clamped to two lines, and left-aligned like a cover teaser rather than a full sentence.

Distinctive UI/interaction patterns:
1. Two-column staggered masonry feed — cards of varied aspect ratio placed into whichever column is currently shorter, with a 10pt column gap and 12pt vertical gap, producing an uneven, browsable magazine rhythm.
2. Lifestyle card as mini magazine cover — a tall cover photo, an optional translucent photo-count/label chip, a punchy two-line title, one to three pastel topic tags, and a byline row with a small avatar, creator name, and like count.
3. Pastel topic-tag system — every card carries one to three soft-background/saturated-text tags (mint, blush, sky, butter, lavender) that together form the app's entire color rhythm outside of yellow.
4. Post detail as a structured magazine article — a swipeable photo carousel, a Poppins title, a creator card with a Follow pill, a styled body with Poppins subheadings and embedded photos, then a tag row and action bar.
5. Yellow rounded-rectangle compose action — the center tab-bar slot for posting is a small yellow rounded rectangle rather than a plain icon, distinguishing it from the other four tab icons.
6. Soft two-layer card shadow — a tight, low-opacity shadow paired with a diffuse, low-opacity shadow so cards appear to lift gently off the page rather than casting a hard drop shadow.

Radius scale: 5pt (tags on cards), 8pt (pastel topic tags, small chips), 14pt (lifestyle cards, embedded article photos), 20pt (bottom sheets, search capsule), 500pt (all buttons, Follow pills, segmented controls), 50% (avatars).
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Build the primary feed as a two-column staggered masonry — never a single-column full-width feed — with cards dropping into whichever column is currently shorter.
2. Use Lemon8 Yellow sparingly — the compose action, the active tab underline, and the primary CTA only — and always pair it with ink text, never white-on-yellow.
3. Give every card one to three pastel topic tags drawn from the fixed five-color set; the tags are the app's color system and should never be omitted or replaced with saturated backgrounds.
4. Keep card titles left-aligned and line-clamped to two lines — they are cover teasers, not full paragraphs, and must never be centered.
5. Set every display headline, screen title, and post title in the geometric display face; keep body copy, card titles, metadata, and tags in the reading-body face — never swap the two.
6. Use the soft two-layer, low-opacity shadow treatment for card elevation — avoid hard, single-layer Material-style shadows.
7. Vary cover-image aspect ratios across cards (square, 3:4, 4:5) to feed the masonry's uneven rhythm — never force every cover to a fixed square.
8. Keep the canvas bright white as the default identity — dark mode exists but is secondary, not the app's core visual identity.
9. Structure the post-detail page like an edited magazine feature (carousel, subheadings, embedded photos) rather than a flat caption-and-comments view.
</house_rules>

- Screens in scope (discovery feed, post detail, topic hub, profile, compose, etc.):

- Existing brand accent that should replace Lemon8 Yellow, if any:
- Accessibility requirements beyond standard Dynamic Type:
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete light/dark color token set (Swift `Color` extension or CSS variables) including the full five-color pastel tag palette.
2. A typographic scale clearly separating the display face (titles/headers) from the body face (cards/meta/tags).
3. The masonry feed layout logic — column-balancing rule, gaps, and how new cards get inserted as the user scrolls.
4. The lifestyle-card component: cover image, optional photo-count chip, title, tag row, and byline.
5. The post-detail component structured as a magazine article — carousel, title, creator card, styled body, tag row, and action bar.
6. The bottom tab bar including the yellow rounded-rectangle compose action.
7. A short note on how the two-layer soft card shadow should be specified in code (values, not just a description).
</what_to_give_me>
